problem: Prior-knowledge-based ObjectNav (offline probability maps, 3D scene graphs) becomes stale when objects are relocated, while purely observation-driven VLM methods (e.g. VLFM) revisit areas and are unstable for small objects with variable context.
motivation: Robots operating long-term in previously visited indoor spaces should exploit accumulated scene knowledge for global guidance while staying adaptive to object rearrangement. The paper's observation is that a prior gives coarse global direction, while real-time VLM evidence validates and corrects it locally.
key_idea: Fuse a scene-graph/commonsense Information Gain Map (global prior) with an online confidence-fused VLM score map (local evidence) in a joint utility that guides RRT-based sub-goal selection and tree expansion.
insight: The prior is treated as informative but potentially biased, so the online VLM weight is set larger than the prior weight. Ablation on the modified HM3D shows the components are complementary: IGM only gives SR 50.87, adding explored-region gating gives 53.92, adding VLM-SM gives 56.28, and the full method reaches 64.91. Explored-region suppression helps most when paired with informative guidance.
method: Information Gain Map (IGM): builds a 3D scene graph (Hydra) from prior exploration; scores each anchor object against the target with ConceptNet Numberbatch cosine similarity (category and spatial-context embeddings) weighted by observation confidence; a GMM turns the anchors into a continuous 2D probability density field.

VLM Score Map (VLM-SM): BLIP-2 image-text similarity against a multi-prompt set of 4 queries (LLM-generated offline, from direct existence to scene context) with weighted aggregation; FOV-based cos² confidence; recursive per-cell confidence-weighted fusion of C_t(x) and V_t(x).
Joint utility: U = λd(1-D(v)) + 1[v∉explored]·(λe·E(v) + λs·S(v)); E is the entropy of the IGM over the unexplored neighborhood and S is the sum of VLM-SM scores over it; λs > λe > λd.

IGV-RRT planner: online RRT with rewiring and root-rewiring under kinematic and collision constraints; selects argmax-utility sub-goal; the explored-region mask suppresses revisits; a global graph of historical vertices gives region-level guidance when local sub-goals are insufficient.
Stuck detection and escape: if displacement in a time window is below a threshold, pick the least-occupied of 8 directions (45° each) and move briefly.
Target detection: GroundingDINO plus MobileSAM for recognition during execution.

setting.backbone: BLIP-2 (frozen) for target relevance; GroundingDINO + MobileSAM (frozen) for detection; ConceptNet Numberbatch embeddings; LLM offline for prompt generation; classical RRT planner
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (plus LiDAR on the AGV) with robot pose
setting.action_space: continuous kinematically feasible RRT paths to sub-goals
setting.simulator: Habitat with HM3D scenes augmented with imported objects (statues, vases); real-world ROS robots
setting.privileged: Prior-time scene snapshot (3D scene graph) from earlier exploration, used to build the IGM; the imported objects are then moved at test time

numbers_note: Only a custom simulation benchmark is reported, with no standard HM3D-ObjNav numbers. The real-world experiments are qualitative, with no quantitative results.
results: On the custom HM3D temporal-change ObjectNav benchmark, IGV-RRT reaches SR 64.91 / SPL 39.28, beating the strongest baseline OneMap (54.38 / 33.23) and VLFM (49.76 / 27.43). Real-world runs on two ROS robots qualitatively show prior-guided approach followed by online correction.
limitations: The IGM is static and cannot be updated online; the authors list updating it as future work.

Evaluation is on a self-constructed benchmark with imported objects (no standard benchmarks); the baselines' setup is not detailed, real-world results are qualitative only, and the number of episodes is not reported.
The utility weights and prompt weights are hand-set, and heavy computation is offloaded to a workstation over ROS.
